findings.reason: §1's remaining work is the launch-count and bit-identity receipt against the existing route, not a new program, so the section must be rewritten to extend `BatchedLabeller` and cite it.
findings.text: §1 ("put the whole slice solve inside one compiled program with a fixed trip budget and masked convergence instead of the host ladder") is already `_make_solver`/`BatchedLabeller`, a dynamic-arg copy of the production fixed trip loop with masked convergence (`finished`) and in-program backtracking factors (`factors`, `choose`, `lax.map(score, candidates)`); the plan proposes rebuilding it

findings.reason: §2 must reconcile with the existing vmap read and either measure/repair the existing pass or state what it replaces, rather than propose a parallel batch read.
findings.text: §2 ("a batch of slices reads in one fixed-shape program") is already `self.operator.read(state_value, requested_value)` inside the vmapped `one()` (`jax.vmap(one)` at line 725, batch sharding at 729), i.e. the topology read already runs once per batch element inside one fixed-shape compiled program

findings.reason: §3 should be scoped as tightening the existing loop's tolerance (default `TURNING_POINT_RELATIVE_TOLERANCE = 0.1`, §3 wants 5 percent) and banking the receipt, not authoring a loop that is present.
findings.text: §3 ("add a Newton outer loop on the achieved shape: re-linearise at the admitted state and iterate until commanded and achieved motions agree to a stated tolerance, still under the admission line search and the 20 kA ceiling") already exists in `solve_shape_inverse`: `current_step_ceiling=CURRENT_STEP_CEILING_A` (20 000 A, line 75), the admission line search (`_moves_toward_command`, `MERIT_RESOLVABLE_STEP_FRACTION`), the secant-refreshed tangent (`_secant_refreshed_tangent`, lines 1511/1546), the bounded loop `while not converged and len(iteration_history) < maximum_iterations` (line 34) and the achieved-over-commanded gain correction

findings.reason: §5 is an extension of this cold-start branch (feed the first read's own read back as its shadow), and it must name that owner rather than describe a new two-pass read.
findings.text: §5 ("read the first iterate twice, the second read shadowed by the first") already has its owner: `_previous_wall_shadow` returns "the prior iterate's wall mask, or no mask on a cold start", and `_residual_shadow_components_from_read` feeds it to `wall_height_shadow_mask` (line 3750); the cold start is the exact gap §5 names

findings.reason: §6 must cite and extend `scripts/labeller_batch/{shard,receipt}.py` rather than propose the job and receipt as new.
findings.text: §6 ("the labeller over the decoder's shot list as one sharded job writing every shot's session as it lands … resumable by shot, with a completion receipt") is already `scripts/labeller_batch`: `shard.py` ("Write forward-solve steering sessions for one shard of MAST shots", `resumed: True` at line 708, per-shot manifest with `converged`/`qualified`/`policy_digest`) and `receipt.py` ("Aggregate forward-labeller shot manifests into a completion receipt", emitting `converged_fraction`, `qualified_fraction`, `gpu_hours`, `policy_digests`)

findings.reason: the honest change is to keep one entry point and fix the throughput of the existing program, so §1/§2 must state whether they add an entry point or amend the existing one.
findings.text: §1 proposes a per-slice compiled program and §2 a batch read as two further entry points beside the existing `solve_batched_labeller`/`BatchedLabeller` one-program-per-batch solver, so the same compiled core (trip loop, backtracking, conditioning, read) gains three public surfaces for one capability

findings.reason: the change is likely one call site in the existing cold-start branch, so §5 should extend it or justify a second path.
findings.text: §5's read-twice adds a second read path over `_previous_wall_shadow`/`_residual_shadow_components_from_read` with no statement of why the existing cold-start branch cannot simply pass the first read's own wall mask to the second read

findings.reason: naming the owners lets the author extend `scripts/labeller_batch/` and the existing read pass instead of forking a second job driver and a second read path.
findings.text: §6 duplicates the decoder-corpus job owner (`shard.py`, plus `receipt.py:2` for the completion receipt) instead of extending it, and §2 duplicates the topology-read owner already held by `BatchedLabeller` (`batched_labeller.py:699`) over `ForwardFluxOperator.read`

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §1 and §2 would add a per-slice compiled program and a batch read as separate entry points beside the existing single one-program-per-batch solver, adding public surface over the same solver core rather than deepening one module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 re-proposes the decoder-corpus shard job and its completion receipt, both already owned by `scripts/labeller_batch/`; §2 re-proposes the topology read already owned by `BatchedLabeller`/`ForwardFluxOperator`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the plan's sections add no CLI option, MCP view, published definition or refusal family, and the one parameter §3 implies (`turning_point_relative_tolerance`) already exists.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan proposes §1 (one compiled program per slice), §2 (a batched on-device topology read), §3 (an achieved-shape Newton outer loop), §5 (a shadow for the cold first iterate) and §6 (a sharded decoder-corpus job with a completion receipt) as new work, each of which already exists in nova and none of which the plan names.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §5's "read the first iterate twice" is a thin layer over the existing cold-start shadow path in `forward_operator.py` without saying why that path cannot simply supply the first read as its own shadow.
